lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.17 - A Compare and write

details: Compare and write checks recall and spelling of the comparatives introduced in this unit through a comparison of two pictures.
Look for confident recall and correct spelling.

“I love puzzles. I can do them very fast! What about you? Are these two pictures the same? Oh, maybe there are a couple of differences. This umbrella is definitely cleaner. What other differences can you spot? And how fast can you find them?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.17 - B. Listen and choose

details: Listen and choose practises listening skills and checks comprehension by asking students to select which picture from each pair matches the audio they hear.
Look for careful listening and confident and correct choices.
“We can use lots of words to describe two pictures. What can we say to describe these picture pairs? Let’s listen and find out!”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.75 - A Find and write

details: Find and write asks students to recall the opposite of each word listed, and then reinforces spelling by having them find it in the wordsearch.
Look for confident and correct naming of each opposite..
“This is one of my favourite word puzzles! We need to find the opposite of each word listed. I really need your help to figure out what words we’re looking for! Let’s see how fast we can do it”

Look for correct choices and note any errors and misconceptions, particularly if repeated.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.18 - Speaking Board Game

details: The board game practises speaking skills and reinforces target language as students ask and answer questions.
Look for turn taking, and confidence asking and answering questions based on the picture cards.
“You’ve worked so hard, it’s time for a game! See how fast you can move up the board, asking and answering questions as you go!”
